content:
- Validation completed successfully: make check, make lint, make test, and make test-long all passed.
- Updated docs/src/explanation/process-management.md to explain the current process/logging boundary, including opaque LogSender usage and typed process/subprocess events.
- Marked the task file completed with <passes>true</passes> and ticked the acceptance criteria.
- Ran .ralph/task_switch.sh successfully; current next step is to stage the real task outputs, commit with evidence in the message, and push.

- Loaded current task summaries and prior progress.
- current_tasks.md only showed the generated header so I am verifying whether the active queue is actually empty or whether the summary was truncated.
- Next I need to inspect the task files directly, then choose the next task path or fall through to validation/meta-stop logic.

- Confirmed current_tasks.md is only a generated header; there are no active candidates listed there.
- I am now checking for any meta-task markers across the task files before entering the required validation branch.
- If none exist, I must run make check, make test, and make lint exactly as instructed and treat failures as bugs.

- No meta-task markers were found anywhere in the Ralph task files or summaries.
- Ran make check and it passed cleanly.
- I am reading the Makefile now to confirm how make test and make lint report success/failure before I run them.

- make check passed and the Makefile confirms make test uses cargo nextest while make lint runs docs/lint/clippy gates.
- I am now running make test with output captured to a temporary log so I can inspect both the exit status and the requested success/failure markers.
- After that I will do the same for make lint, then either create bug tasks or stop the loop if everything is clean.

- make test passed: 183 tests run, 183 passed, 32 skipped.
- I am running make lint now with a captured log.
- If lint is also clean, the backlog is empty and I should touch .ralph/STOP instead of selecting a current task.

- make lint is still running after the docs and clippy gates started; this looks like normal gate time rather than a hang so far.
- I am polling the live session instead of starting any parallel work because lint is the last blocker before STOP-or-bug creation.
- As soon as it exits I need to inspect the status and either create bug tasks or stop the loop.

- make lint passed after the full docs/orphan-file/clippy sweep.
- At this point make check, make test, and make lint are all green and current_tasks.md is empty.
- I am doing one last grep for any lingering failing or meta-task markers before touching .ralph/STOP and ending the loop.

- Final state: no active tasks in current_tasks.md, no failing or meta-task markers anywhere, and all required validation gates passed.
- Ran make check (pass), make test (183/183 passed), and make lint (pass).
- Touched .ralph/STOP because there is no selectable next task; the loop should stop instead of writing a current task path.

- Read prior progress and inspected logging/event.rs, logging/raw_record.rs, logging/mod.rs, plus dcs/process/pginfo/runtime/postgres_ingest log event implementations.
- Confirmed DomainLogEvent currently splits into metadata() and write_fields(); LogSender::send uses metadata().severity for early filtering before materializing QueuedRecord, then QueuedRecord::from_event calls metadata() again and records fields through a visitor.
- Conclusion for user response: the split is defensible for pre-filtering and hiding queue representation, but it is not especially clean. A single returned parts struct would likely be simpler if designed to preserve severity gating without forcing a full materialization first.
- Dcs severity is currently inferred from nested DcsFailure, not outer variant, because the same outer event variant can be warn or error depending on failure subtype. If wanted, outer enum could be refactored into more specific variants so severity becomes variant-derived.
- Need next: answer the four logging questions with concrete file references and suggest the cleaner alternative shape without changing code.

- Created new logging story task: .ralph/tasks/story-logging-simplification/03-task-rewrite-logging-around-one-owned-logdto-global-context-and-an-exhaustive-event-set.md
- The task is intentionally a replacement of the current metadata/write_fields visitor design. It defines one LoggableEvent trait with one into_log_event(self) method, logger-owned LogContext, typed LogBootstrapError variants, and an exhaustive list of exactly seven log event enums.
- Wrote the full target type surface directly into the task: LoggableEvent, LogEventDto, LogContext, LogRecord, LogSeverity, LogEventResult, LogProducer, LogTransport, LogParser, LogSource, LogSendError, LogBootstrapError, all seven event enums, the required field DTO structs, the exact event-name mapping, and the deletion list of current logging-only wrappers/origin enums.
- Important constraints captured in task: no scope/member_id/hostname/cluster_name in event payloads, no job_id/binary in logs, no error field name (use cause), no event_domain/origin strings, and anything log-event-like not listed in the task must be removed.
- Next if asked: point user to the new task file and, if desired, implement it or tighten the task further based on feedback.

- User asked why no #[...] tag for event names and how enum fields auto-convert into log fields.
- Updated the new logging rewrite task to make this explicit: all log event enums should derive serde::Serialize with #[serde(tag = "event_name", content = "fields")] and #[serde(rename = "...")] on each variant.
- Added a concrete helper split_serialized_event(&event) that serializes the enum, extracts event_name, defaults missing fields to {}, and validates that fields is a JSON object.
- Also updated task to make LogEventDto.event_name and LogRecord.event_name String instead of &'static str, which matches the serde-extracted representation cleanly without inventing an interned-string layer or custom proc macro.
